chapter.title: Coming From Elsewhere
chapter.para: Programs written for ooRexx's other ways to .NET and COM run on the bridge, unchanged or with small changes.

section.title: Programs Written for CLR.CLS
section.para: You want to run a program written for BSF4ooRexx's CLR.CLS.

example.title: Programs Written for CLR.CLS
example.programlisting:
console = clr.import("System.Console") console~WriteLine("Hello from CLR.CLS") sb = .clr~new("System.Text.StringBuilder", "ab") say sb~Append("c")~ToString pp(sb~Length)
::requires CLR.CLS

section.para: How it works. The bridge has its own CLR.CLS, a compatibility package over net.cls: a program that requires it runs on .NET 8 or later, without Java. Its rules are CLR.CLS's where they differ (a whole number goes as an Int32).
See also Reference, Programs Written for CLR.CLS.

section.title: From BSF4ooRexx
section.para: You want to write for .NET what you write for Java with BSF4ooRexx.

How it works. The shape is the same: bsf.import("java.lang.Math") is .net~System~Math; .bsf~new(...) is type~new(...); arrays are Rexx Arrays from 1; enum values are objects; box and unbox take the same indicators; a Rexx object given to Java as a proxy (BsfCreateRexxProxy) is .net~handler(obj, "MESSAGE") for one method, or a class that .net~extend makes implement an interface; and the event thread's runLater methods are BSF4ooRexx's. In .NET, Rexx's start and send reach the .NET member of that name when there is one, so no bsf.dispatch is needed for them.
See also Reference, Relation to BSF4ooRexx and the Sister Bridges.

section.title: From OLEObject
section.para: You want to move an ooRexx OLE program to the bridge, to use .NET in it too.

How it works. Replace .OLEObject~new(progID) with .net~createObject(progID), and add ::requires "net.cls": the messages are the same. Constants are .net~getConstant(o, name); an argument by reference, a .net~ref; events, o~Name += .net~handler(object, message); and where the program waited for events with SysSleep, it waits with .net~nextEvent(seconds). The reference's table has the rest, and the project's samples/oorexx-ole has ooRexx's own OLE samples, so changed.
See also Reference, COM Objects (Windows), From OLEObject.

section.title: How Fast Is It?
section.para: You want to know what a call costs.

How it works. A call from Rexx to .NET costs a few microseconds: a property read about 3, a method with overloads to choose from 6 to 10, a callback from .NET into Rexx about 6 to 15. Names are looked up once and remembered, so keep a type in a variable in a loop (m = .net~System~Math) rather than walking the namespaces each time. When you measure, measure warm: .NET compiles a method again, faster, after its first tens of thousands of calls, so a cold loop measures the compiler. .net~handleCount shows the .NET objects Rexx holds: a number that keeps growing means proxies kept somewhere.
See also Reference, Names and Messages.
